hints: Focus on the anion in each compound, as Group 2 solubility follows clear trends for chlorides, carbonates, hydroxides and sulfates.
Remember that all Group 2 chlorides are soluble, while all Group 2 carbonates are insoluble in water.
Now apply the opposite trends for the other two anions: hydroxides get more soluble down the group, but sulfates get less soluble, so check each list for one insoluble member.
walkthrough:
**Recall the easy rules first**

All Group 2 chlorides are soluble in water, and all Group 2 carbonates are insoluble. This lets you quickly test many options.

Rule: $\text{Group 2 chlorides = soluble, Group 2 carbonates = insoluble}$

**Recall the hydroxide trend**

Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2. Magnesium hydroxide is insoluble, calcium hydroxide is only sparingly soluble, while strontium hydroxide and barium hydroxide are soluble.

Trend: $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 < \text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2$ in solubility

**Recall the sulfate trend**

Sulfate solubility decreases down Group 2, the opposite trend. Magnesium sulfate is very soluble, calcium sulfate is sparingly soluble, while strontium sulfate and barium sulfate are insoluble.

Trend: $\text{MgSO}_4 > \text{CaSO}_4 > \text{SrSO}_4 > \text{BaSO}_4$ in solubility

**Test each list**

Barium chloride is soluble, barium hydroxide is soluble (bottom of group), and magnesium sulfate is soluble (top of group). So that list has three soluble compounds, while every other list contains at least one carbonate, insoluble hydroxide or insoluble sulfate.

options.A: Barium chloride is soluble, but calcium carbonate is insoluble because all Group 2 carbonates are insoluble. Magnesium hydroxide is also insoluble as it is at the top of the hydroxide trend. One soluble out of three is not enough.
options.B: Barium hydroxide is soluble and calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble, but strontium carbonate is insoluble. Students sometimes remember the hydroxide trend correctly but forget that all carbonates of Group 2 are insoluble, so this list fails.
options.C: All three are soluble. Barium chloride is soluble as all chlorides are soluble. Barium hydroxide is soluble as hydroxides become more soluble down the group. Magnesium sulfate is soluble as sulfates become more soluble up the group.
options.D: None of these count as fully soluble. Barium sulfate is famously insoluble, calcium sulfate is only sparingly soluble, and magnesium hydroxide is insoluble. This is the classic trap if the sulfate and hydroxide trends are mixed up.
